I've been farming this land since I was young, watching my father do the same. The land here in Quzhou is good flat ground on the North China Plain. Everyone around me grows winter wheat followed by summer maize — that rotation feeds my family and earns steady income. I have about 12 mu of cultivated land. There is no reason to try something unfamiliar this year. Prices for wheat and maize have been stable, and I know exactly how to manage these crops. Cotton is too much trouble and the market has been bad. Vegetables need too much attention and I don't have the connections to sell them well.

For wheat, I plant in October and harvest in June. I'll use an improved variety — the county station recommends 矮抗58 and I've used it for years with good results. I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting and urea at jointing. I always do four irrigations: the winter water to protect roots from freezing, jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray herbicide early and hit the aphids and powdery mildew once before harvest.

For maize, I plant immediately after the wheat comes off in June. No sense wasting time. I use郑单958 hybrid seed — everyone uses it and it doesn't fail. I direct-seed without deep tillage to save moisture and time. I apply urea in two splits. Usually I only need one or two waterings if the summer rains cooperate.
